notes.meaning: Eleazar the high priest, Joshua, and the tribal leaders gathered to divide the land of Canaan among the people. Eleazar is named first because dividing the land involved appealing directly to God, making it a sacred religious act. God had already chosen these specific leaders years earlier through Moses so everyone would know the distribution was fair. We can trust God to guide those who lead his people with fairness and care.

The land for the remaining nine and a half tribes was assigned by casting lots, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. Casting lots let God himself choose each tribe's home, which stopped jealousy and arguing before they could start. The lots placed each tribe in the exact general area that Jacob and Moses had foretold long before. Believers can rest knowing that God wisely directs every part of their lives.

Moses had already given territories east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. The tribe of Levi received no large province of land like the others did. God set the Levites apart to serve him in worship and holy duties, so they were not to be tied down by managing a large region.

Joseph's two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, were counted as two full tribes, which kept the total number of land-owning tribes at twelve even without Levi. The Levites still needed places to live, so they were given specific towns spread across all the tribal lands, along with open fields for their farm animals. This provided for the priests while ensuring they lived among the people to teach them God's ways.

The Israelites obeyed the commands the Lord had given through Moses and began the work of dividing the land. They set up the proper procedures, measurements, and leadership needed to carry out God's plan in an orderly way. Doing God's work requires careful obedience to the directions he has provided.

Leaders from the tribe of Judah came with Caleb to meet Joshua at Gilgal before the lots were drawn. Caleb reminded Joshua of the promise God had spoken through Moses at Kadesh-barnea regarding the two of them. Because Caleb was one of the leaders dividing the land, he brought his fellow tribal leaders along so everything would be open and honest.

Caleb recalled that he was forty years old when Moses sent him to explore the land of Canaan. When he returned, he gave an honest report based on what he truly believed in his heart, rather than giving in to fear or trying to please the crowd. He spoke with complete sincerity because he trusted God's promise to give them the land.

The other ten spies brought back a terrifying report that made the Israelites lose heart and melt with fear. In contrast, Caleb stood firm and followed the Lord completely, refusing to let the panic of the crowd shake his faith. True loyalty to God often means standing alone when everyone around us gives way to fear.

Moses made a solemn promise on that day that the land Caleb had walked upon would belong to him and his family forever. This reward was promised because Caleb had followed the Lord God with his whole heart. God does not forget the faithfulness of his people, even when years pass before the promise is fulfilled.

God kept Caleb alive for forty-five years after making that promise, through thirty-eight years of wandering in the desert and seven years of war in Canaan. All the other men of his generation had died in the wilderness because of their unbelief, but Caleb was now eighty-five years old and thriving. He gave all the credit to the Lord for preserving his life and health for so long.

At eighty-five, Caleb was just as strong for daily duties and for battle as he had been when Moses first sent him out. Most people grow weak in old age, but God gave Caleb exceptional physical strength and energy so he could complete his mission. He was not looking for an easy retirement, but was ready to fight for the inheritance God promised him.

Caleb asked Joshua to give him the rugged hill country of Hebron, where giant warriors lived in large, walled cities. Even though it was the most dangerous and difficult place in the land, Caleb was confident that with the Lord's help he could drive them out. He chose the hardest task not out of pride, but out of total dependence on God's power.

Joshua blessed Caleb and granted him Hebron as his personal inheritance. This blessing was a prayer asking God to help Caleb defeat the giants and take hold of the land. Joshua publicly honored Caleb's courage and held him up as an inspiring example for all Israel to follow.

Hebron remained in the family of Caleb because he had followed the Lord, the God of Israel, with his whole heart. His lasting reward came as a direct result of his lifelong obedience and steadfast faith. God honors those who stay true to him through every season of life.

The city of Hebron had formerly been named Kiriath-arba after Arba, who was the greatest and most famous warrior among the giant Anakim. Once Caleb received his territory and the main resistance was broken, the land entered a time of rest from war. God brought peace so his people could begin settling safely into the homes he had provided.
